Add a RATE column to a NONMEM dataset

Source: R/nm_data_previsual.R
nm_add_rate.Rd

Reads the CSV verbatim (all columns as character) so that nothing is reformatted, adds a RATE column based on the dosing records, and writes a new file. The original columns (values, format, '#ID' header) are kept unchanged.

Usage

nm_add_rate(
  file,
  output_file = NULL,
  sep = ",",
  dose_value = -2,
  base_value = 0,
  after = "AMT",
  dose_cmt = NULL,
  cmt_col = NULL,
  evid_col = NULL,
  amt_col = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

file

Path to the original CSV.

output_file

Name (or path) of the output CSV. NULL (default) -> "<base>_rate.csv" in the same directory as file. If only a file name is given (no directory), it is placed next to the source file. (Formerly out_file, still accepted with a warning.)

sep

Column separator (default ",").

dose_value

RATE value on the targeted dosing records: -2 (default, estimated duration) or -1 (estimated rate).

base_value

RATE value on all other records (default 0).

after

Name of the column after which RATE is inserted (default "AMT"). NULL = added as the last column.

dose_cmt

CMT value(s) identifying the route(s) that receive dose_value. NULL (default): all dosing records receive dose_value (single-route dataset). E.g. dose_cmt = 1 to affect only the oral depot, leaving IV boluses (other CMT) at base_value.

cmt_col

Name of the CMT column (default: auto-detected). Required only when dose_cmt is supplied.

evid_col

Name of the EVID column (default: auto-detected).

amt_col

Name of the AMT column (default: auto-detected; used only when no EVID column is found).

overwrite

If TRUE, overwrite an existing RATE column (default FALSE: the function stops if RATE already exists).

verbose

Print a diagnostic report (default TRUE).

...

Former argument name, accepted with a warning until version 1.0.

Value

The path of the written file (invisibly).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Single route: RATE=-2 on all doses -> data_nmol_rate.csv
nm_add_rate("C:/nm74g64/run/Bienvenu/data_nmol.csv")

# Estimated rate rather than duration
nm_add_rate("data.csv", dose_value = -1)

# Multiple routes: -2 only on the oral depot (CMT=1),
# IV boluses (CMT=2) keep RATE=0
nm_add_rate("data.csv", dose_cmt = 1)

# Chosen output name (placed next to the source file)
nm_add_rate("data.csv", output_file = "data_dur.csv")
} # }
